# Room-by-Room Packing Checklist with Declutter Tips

**How this works:** Each room gets a declutter pass first, then a packing pass. I've split packing into two waves — **Early Pack** (non-essentials, 4–6 weeks out) and **Final Pack** (last week). Every box should be labeled with: **Room name + contents summary + box number + FRAGILE if applicable.** Keep a running numbered inventory on your phone or a clipboard.

---

## 🍳 KITCHEN

**Responsible:** J (joint) — this is the biggest room and goes faster with two people
**Estimated time:** 4–6 hours total (split across 2–3 sessions)
**Priority:** HIGH — start early because it has the most items and the most declutter potential

---

### Declutter Pass (do this first, 1–1.5 hrs)

- [ ] Pull everything out of each cabinet one shelf at a time
- [ ] **Toss:** chipped or cracked dishes, melted spatulas, rusty utensils, stained tupperware without lids, expired spices and food, duplicate can openers, mystery takeout sauce packets, anything sticky or broken
- [ ] **Donate:** duplicate sets of dishes, appliances you haven't used in 12 months (bread maker, fondue pot, juicer), cookbooks you've never opened, excess mugs and water bottles, mismatched silverware
- [ ] **Sell:** high-value small appliances in good condition (KitchenAid, Instant Pot, cast iron you won't ship)
- [ ] **Give to neighbors:** open pantry items, spices, cleaning supplies, half-used rolls of foil and wrap

**Declutter gut-check:** If you have more than one of something and you haven't used the second one in a year, the second one goes. Moving a $12 blender 2,400 miles costs more in space and weight than replacing it.

---

### Early Pack — 4 to 6 weeks out (1.5–2 hrs)

| Box | Contents | Packing Tips |
|---|---|---|
| K-1 | Baking supplies: cake pans, muffin tins, cookie sheets, rolling pin, mixing bowls | Nest bowls. Put parchment paper between pans to prevent scratching. |
| K-2 | Specialty appliances: stand mixer, blender, food processor | Original boxes are ideal. Otherwise wrap in towels and pack snugly so nothing shifts. Remove blades, wrap separately in cardboard and tape, and label "SHARP." |
| K-3 | Entertaining items: serving platters, punch bowl, wine glasses, candle holders | Wrap each glass individually in packing paper. Place upright in cells or stuff paper between them. Mark FRAGILE on all sides and top. |
| K-4 | Cookbooks, recipe binders, decorative items | Small box. Books are heavy — never fill a large box with only books. |
| K-5 | Seasonal or rarely used items: holiday cookie cutters, canning supplies, specialty gadgets | One small or medium box. If you hesitate, ask yourself when you last used it. |

---

### Final Pack — last 3 to 5 days (1.5–2 hrs)

| Box | Contents | Packing Tips |
|---|---|---|
| K-6 | Everyday dishes: plates, bowls, mugs (the set you kept out) | Stack plates vertically like records — they break less. Wrap each piece. Pad the bottom and top of the box with crumpled paper or towels. Mark FRAGILE. |
| K-7 | Pots, pans, lids, daily utensils, cutting board | Nest pots. Put a layer of paper between each. Wrap lids together. Rubber-band utensils. |
| K-8 | Knives, sharp tools, peeler, grater | Wrap each blade in cardboard and tape it shut. Label "SHARP" on the outside. Or use blade guards. |
| K-9 | Small countertop appliances: toaster, coffee maker, kettle | Empty water from coffee maker. Wrap cords and tape them to the appliance so they don't swing. |
| K-10 | Under-sink items: dish soap, sponges, trash bags, cleaning supplies | Zip-lock any liquids. Pack upright. Label "CLEANING — OPEN EARLY." |
| K-11 | Junk drawer and miscellaneous | Zip-lock small items (batteries, twist ties, rubber bands, takeout menus). Toss what you don't need. |
| K-LAST | Pantry food (non-perishable, sealed) | Use a sturdy small box — cans are heavy. If the item costs less than $3 to replace, consider leaving it. |

**Labeling rule for kitchen:** Mark every kitchen box with a **K** prefix and number. Write "FRAGILE" on any box with glass or ceramic. Write "OPEN FIRST" on the box with coffee maker, mugs, paper towels, and snacks — you'll want that box within 10 minutes of arriving.

---

## 🛋️ LIVING ROOM

**Responsible:** J (joint) — partner focuses on electronics and cables, you focus on decor and shelving
**Estimated time:** 3–4 hours total (split across 2 sessions)
**Priority:** MEDIUM-HIGH — lots of fragile items and electronics that need careful wrapping

---

### Declutter Pass (do this first, 45 min–1 hr)

- [ ] Pull everything off shelves and surfaces
- [ ] **Toss:** dead batteries, old magazines and catalogs, dried-out markers, broken picture frames, candles burned to the nub, tangled cords to unknown devices, dead remotes, instruction manuals (they're all online now)
- [ ] **Donate:** DVDs and Blu-rays you've ripped or never rewatch, board games missing pieces, books you won't reread, throw pillows and blankets you don't love, decor that doesn't fit your taste anymore
- [ ] **Sell:** electronics in good condition (speakers, gaming consoles, monitors), furniture you're not moving
- [ ] **Recycle:** old electronics at a certified e-waste drop-off, not in the trash

**Declutter gut-check:** Hold each decorative item and ask: "Would I buy this again today?" If no, it doesn't earn a spot on the truck.

---

### Early Pack — 4 to 6 weeks out (1–1.5 hrs)

| Box | Contents | Packing Tips |
|---|---|---|
| LR-1 | Books and coffee table books | Small boxes only. Fill gaps with packing paper so books don't shift. Spine down for paperbacks. |
| LR-2 | Framed photos and wall art (non-high-value) | Wrap each frame in bubble wrap. Place cardboard corners on frame edges. Stand upright in box like a record — never lay flat and stack. Mark FRAGILE and "THIS SIDE UP." |
| LR-3 | Decorative items: vases, sculptures, candles, bookends | Wrap individually. Fill all empty space so nothing moves when you shake the box. If it rattles, add more paper. |
| LR-4 | Board games, puzzles, cards | Rubber-band game boxes shut. Bag loose pieces. Medium box. |
| LR-5 | Shelving hardware, brackets, curtain rods, hooks | Zip-lock all screws and bolts. Tape the bag to the item it belongs to. Take a photo of your curtain rod bracket setup before removing — you'll forget the spacing. |
| LR-6 | Throw blankets, decorative pillows, couch covers (extras) | Use these as padding in other boxes or stuff them into garbage bags to save box space. They're great cushioning for fragile items. |

---

### Final Pack — last 3 to 5 days (1–1.5 hrs)

| Box | Contents | Packing Tips |
|---|---|---|
| LR-7 (P responsible) | TV, soundbar, streaming devices, remotes | Original TV box is ideal. If you don't have it, buy a TV box or wrap in moving blankets. Never lay a flat-screen face-down. Transport upright. Take a photo of the back of the TV and all cable connections before unplugging. Zip-lock all remotes together with batteries removed. |
| LR-8 (P responsible) | Gaming console, controllers, cables | Wrap the console in a towel. Coil each cable separately and secure with a twist-tie or velcro strap. Label which cable goes to what. |
| LR-9 (P responsible) | Router, modem, power strips, surge protectors, charging cables | Label every cable with masking tape and a marker: "router power," "HDMI TV," etc. You will not remember later. Zip-lock small adapters together. |
| LR-10 | Lamps and lampshades | Remove bulbs and pack them separately in socks or bubble wrap. Remove shades and nest them in a large box with paper stuffed inside to hold shape. Wrap lamp bases in bubble wrap. |
| LR-11 | Last decorative items, couch throw, everyday blanket | Soft items — use as padding in other boxes or pack in a trash bag. |

**Labeling rule for living room:** Mark every box with an **LR** prefix and number. Mark electronics boxes with "ELECTRONICS — HANDLE WITH CARE" and an arrow pointing up. Mark the box with the router "OPEN FIRST — INTERNET" so you can get online quickly.

---

### Furniture Notes (Living Room)

| Item | Tip |
|---|---|
| Couch / sectional | Remove legs if possible. Bag and tape legs and bolts together. Wrap in moving blankets or stretch wrap. Measure your Oregon doorways before the truck arrives — couches are the number one item that doesn't fit. |
| Bookshelves | Remove shelves. Wrap shelves together with cardboard between them. Bag shelf pins and tape to the unit. Wrap the frame in blankets. |
| TV stand / media console | Empty completely. Remove glass doors. Wrap glass separately and label FRAGILE. Zip-lock all hardware. |
| Coffee / side tables | Wrap legs and corners with bubble wrap or pool noodles cut to size. Glass tops should be wrapped separately and transported upright. |
| Area rugs | Roll tightly (don't fold). Secure with stretch wrap or rope. Stand upright in the truck. |
| Curtains / rods | Fold curtains and pack in a bag. Tape rod hardware to the rod. |

---

## General Packing Principles (Apply to Every Room)

**Box rules:**
- Heavy items in small boxes, light items in large boxes — no exceptions
- Fill every box completely so it doesn't crush when stacked, but don't over-pack so it bursts
- Tape the bottom of every box with an H-pattern (one strip lengthwise, two strips across) — the single-strip bottom is the number one cause of box blowouts
- Never pack liquids, flammables, or perishables in the moving truck

**Labeling system:**
- Room abbreviation + box number + 2–3 word contents + FRAGILE if applicable
- Example: **K-6 / Everyday Dishes / FRAGILE**
- Write on two sides and the top of every box
- Use a different color marker or tape for each room if you want visual sorting

**Inventory:**
- Keep a simple numbered list on your phone (Google Sheets or Notes app)
- Format: Box number → contents summary → value estimate for insurance
- Photograph the inside of each box before taping it shut — this takes 5 seconds and can save an insurance claim

**Weight test:** If you can't comfortably lift the box to waist height, it's too heavy. Repack.

---

*Ready for the next rooms when you are — I'll cover bedroom, bathroom, office/study, closets and storage, garage/outdoor, and laundry/utility. Want me to continue?*

# Room-by-Room Packing Checklist (Continued)

---

## 🛏️ MASTER BEDROOM

**Responsible:** J (joint) — each person packs their own clothes; partner handles furniture disassembly
**Estimated time:** 3–4 hours total (split across 2 sessions)
**Priority:** MEDIUM — you live in this room until the last day, so most of it is a final-week pack

---

### Declutter Pass (45 min–1 hr)

- [ ] Empty every drawer, shelf, and nightstand completely
- [ ] **Toss:** single earrings, broken jewelry, stretched-out hair ties, old phone cases, dried-up lotions, empty notebooks, dead pens, charging cables for devices you no longer own, worn-out pillows (if you can fold a pillow in half and it doesn't spring back, it's dead)
- [ ] **Donate:** clothes you haven't worn in 12 months, books you've finished and won't reread, spare bedding sets beyond two, lamps or decor that won't suit Oregon
- [ ] **Sell:** quality furniture you're not moving (bed frame, dresser, nightstands)

**Declutter gut-check:** Try the reverse hanger trick — turn all hangers backward now. Anything still backward on packing day hasn't been worn and probably shouldn't make the trip.

---

### Early Pack — 4 to 6 weeks out (1–1.5 hrs)

| Box | Contents | Packing Tips |
|---|---|---|
| BR-1 | Out-of-season clothes | Use wardrobe boxes for hanging clothes if your budget allows ($10–$15 each). Otherwise, leave clothes on hangers, poke hangers through a small hole in a trash bag from the bottom, and tie the bag at the top — instant garment bag. |
| BR-2 | Extra bedding: spare sheets, comforter, bed skirt, mattress pad | Vacuum-seal bags save massive space. Roll rather than fold to reduce wrinkles. These also make great truck padding. |
| BR-3 | Jewelry, watches, keepsakes, sentimental items | Carry high-value jewelry in your personal bag in the car, not the truck. Use egg cartons or ice cube trays for small items like rings and earrings. Photograph everything for insurance. |
| BR-4 | Bookshelf items, photos, decor, nightstand extras | Wrap frames individually. Use socks to pad small items. |

---

### Final Pack — last 3 to 5 days (1–1.5 hrs)

| Box | Contents | Packing Tips |
|---|---|---|
| BR-5 (M) | Your remaining everyday clothes (1 suitcase worth stays out) | Leave your moving-day outfit and 3–4 days of clothes in your suitcase in the car. Everything else gets boxed. |
| BR-6 (P) | Partner's remaining everyday clothes | Same approach. |
| BR-7 | Alarm clock, phone stand, reading lamp, books in progress, chargers | Small box. Label "OPEN FIRST — BEDROOM." |
| BR-8 | Hangers (empty) | Bundle 10–15 hangers with a rubber band or zip-tie. Pack in a trash bag or wardrobe box. They tangle horribly loose. |

**🐕 Pet note:** If the dog sleeps in your bedroom, pack their secondary bed or blanket in BR-2 early. Keep their primary bed out until moving morning, then put it in the car — the familiar smell reduces travel anxiety.

### Furniture Notes

| Item | Tip |
|---|---|
| Mattress | Buy a mattress bag ($5–$15). Slide it on and tape shut. Transport on its side in the truck. Never lay a mattress flat with boxes on top — it damages the internal structure. |
| Bed frame | Disassemble. Zip-lock all bolts, screws, and Allen keys and tape the bag to the headboard. Photograph the assembly before taking it apart. Keep the Allen key accessible in your basic toolkit. |
| Dresser | You can leave lightweight clothes (socks, t-shirts) in drawers to save box space — wrap the dresser in stretch wrap to keep drawers shut. Remove heavy items. Never move a dresser with the drawers full of heavy items — it destroys the joints. |
| Nightstands | Empty completely. Wrap edges. Zip-lock hardware if legs remove. |
| Mirror | Tape a large X across the glass with painter's tape (reduces shatter spread). Wrap in bubble wrap and cardboard. Mark FRAGILE and "DO NOT LAY FLAT." |

---

## 🚿 BATHROOM

**Responsible:** M (me) handles the main bathroom; P handles the second bathroom or en-suite
**Estimated time:** 1.5–2 hours total (most of it is final-week)
**Priority:** MEDIUM — small room but lots of liquids and sharp items that need careful handling

---

### Declutter Pass (30 min)

- [ ] Pull everything out of the medicine cabinet, under the sink, and all drawers
- [ ] **Toss:** expired medications (take to a pharmacy for safe disposal, don't flush), expired sunscreen and cosmetics, dried-up nail polish, nearly empty bottles, rusty razors, stiff toothbrushes, crusty tubes of anything, hotel shampoo you've been hoarding
- [ ] **Donate:** unopened toiletries and products you tried once and didn't like (shelters often accept these)
- [ ] **Leave behind / gift to neighbors:** half-used cleaning products, bulky cheap items not worth moving

**Declutter gut-check:** Toiletries are the number one category people over-pack. If it costs less than $5 to replace at a Target in Oregon, leave it behind. Your truck space per pound is worth more.

---

### Early Pack — 4 to 6 weeks out (20–30 min)

| Box | Contents | Packing Tips |
|---|---|---|
| BA-1 | Spare towels, washcloths, bath mats beyond one set each | Vacuum-seal or use as packing padding in fragile boxes. |
| BA-2 | Medicine cabinet overflow: backup meds, first-aid supplies, heating pad, humidifier | Zip-lock all pills and liquids individually. Keep current daily meds out. |
| BA-3 | Under-sink backup supplies: extra cleaning products, toilet paper bulk packs, extra soap | Only pack what's worth the weight. Sealed items only — no half-used bleach bottles in the truck. |

---

### Final Pack — last 2 to 3 days (30–45 min)

| Box | Contents | Packing Tips |
|---|---|---|
| BA-4 | Remaining towels (keep 1 per person plus 1 for the dog in the car) | Use towels to wrap bathroom fragile items to save paper. |
| BA-5 | Hair dryer, flat iron, electric razor, grooming tools | Let heat tools cool completely. Wrap cords and tape to the tool. Pack in a padded box. |
| BA-6 | Shower curtain, rings, bath accessories, soap dishes, wastebasket | Wash and dry the curtain before packing. Zip-lock the rings. |
| BA-LAST | Daily toiletries: toothbrushes, toothpaste, deodorant, face wash, shampoo, razor | Pack this into your personal suitcase in the car, not a moving box. You'll need it at every overnight stop. |

**🐕 Pet note:** Dog shampoo, flea/tick treatment, ear cleaner, and grooming tools — pack in the dog travel bag if you might need them on the road, or in BA-2 early if you won't.

**Labeling rule for bathroom:** Mark all boxes with a **BA** prefix. Write "LIQUIDS — KEEP UPRIGHT" on any box containing bottles. Double-bag anything that could leak.

---

## 💻 OFFICE / STUDY

**Responsible:** Each person packs their own work setup; joint for shared items (printer, shredder, filing cabinet)
**Estimated time:** 2.5–3.5 hours total (split across 2 sessions)
**Priority:** HIGH — electronics and documents need careful handling, and work-from-home setups need to come back online fast in Oregon

---

### Declutter Pass (45 min–1 hr)

- [ ] Empty every drawer, file folder, and shelf
- [ ] **Toss:** old tax records beyond 7 years (shred them), outdated manuals, dead pens and markers, random cables and adapters you can't identify, broken staplers, sticky notes that have lost their stick, dried-up ink cartridges
- [ ] **Shred and recycle:** old bank statements, pay stubs older than current-year, pre-approved credit card mailers, documents with personal info you no longer need
- [ ] **Donate:** books, office supplies in excess, old monitors and keyboards (working condition to Goodwill or e-waste)
- [ ] **Digitize:** scan important paper documents and save to your Move cloud folder before packing the originals

**Declutter gut-check:** Most people move 2–3 file drawers of paper they never look at again. Be ruthless. If it's not a legal document, tax record from the last 7 years, or irreplaceable sentimental item, scan it and shred it.

---

### Early Pack — 4 to 6 weeks out (1–1.5 hrs)

| Box | Contents | Packing Tips |
|---|---|---|
| OF-1 | Reference books, binders, non-active files | Small boxes for heavy files. Never put more than a ream's worth of paper in a single box. |
| OF-2 | Office supplies: stapler, tape, pens, envelopes, sticky notes, scissors | One medium box. Zip-lock small items. Put scissors in a cardboard sheath. |
| OF-3 | Printer, scanner, shredder | Remove ink cartridges and pack them in a zip-lock (they leak). Put a piece of tape over the paper tray so it doesn't open. Original box if you have it. |
| OF-4 | Spare cables, adapters, chargers, USB hubs, docking stations | Label every cable with masking tape before coiling. Put each cable group in a zip-lock: "monitor cables," "phone chargers," "audio." You will thank yourself in Oregon. |

---

### Final Pack — last 3 to 5 days (1–1.5 hrs)

| Box | Contents | Packing Tips |
|---|---|---|
| OF-5 (M) | Your computer, monitor, keyboard, mouse | Photograph your desk setup and all cable connections before unplugging. Original boxes are ideal for monitors. If not, wrap the monitor in a towel, then bubble wrap, and place upright in a box. Never lay a monitor flat with items on top. Mark FRAGILE. |
| OF-6 (P) | Partner's computer, monitor, keyboard, mouse | Same approach. |
| OF-7 | Desk lamp, whiteboard, bulletin board, wall calendar, desk accessories | Wrap lamp shade separately. Remove whiteboard markers (they dry out in heat — put in a zip-lock in the car's climate-controlled cabin). |
| OF-8 | Active files and documents you need soon | Label "OPEN FIRST — OFFICE" so you can find tax docs, warranty papers, and work files quickly. |

**Critical reminder:** Back up all computers to an external drive and/or cloud before packing. Keep the backup drive in the car, not the truck. If the truck is lost or delayed, your data survives.

### Furniture Notes

| Item | Tip |
|---|---|
| Desk | Remove drawers if possible. Wrap edges. If it's an L-shaped desk, check whether it disassembles — most do. Bag hardware. |
| Office chair | Lower the chair to its lowest position. If the base detaches, remove it. Wrap in stretch wrap. Office chairs are awkward in a truck — load last and wedge between items. |
| Filing cabinet | Empty it completely. Lock the drawers or tape them shut. Move empty. |
| Bookshelves | Same as living room: remove shelves, bag pins, wrap the frame. |

---

## 👗 CLOSETS AND STORAGE AREAS

**Responsible:** J (joint) — each person handles their own closet, joint for shared storage (hall closet, coat closet, linen closet)
**Estimated time:** 2–3 hours total
**Priority:** HIGH for declutter (this is where the most junk hides), MEDIUM for packing

---

### Declutter Pass (1–1.5 hrs — this is the biggest declutter opportunity in the house)

- [ ] Pull everything out of every closet, shelf, and storage bin
- [ ] **Toss:** broken umbrellas, single gloves, wire hangers (recycle at dry cleaner), worn-out shoes, old shopping bags, expired batteries, outgrown or stained clothing
- [ ] **Donate:** coats and shoes in good condition you haven't worn in a year, board games, luggage you're replacing, holiday decor you're tired of, outgrown pet items
- [ ] **Sell:** quality outerwear, name-brand shoes and bags, sports equipment in good condition
- [ ] **Gift:** sentimental items to friends or family who'd appreciate them more than a box in your Oregon garage

**Declutter gut-check:** Storage closets are the number one place where "I might need this someday" items accumulate. If you've stored it for 2+ years without touching it, the answer is no, you won't need it. Let it go.

---

### Packing (1–1.5 hrs, mostly early pack)

| Box | Contents | Packing Tips |
|---|---|---|
| CL-1 | Coats, jackets, formalwear | Wardrobe boxes or the trash-bag-over-hangers method. Keep one rain jacket out for the drive. Oregon will welcome you with drizzle. |
| CL-2 | Shoes | Stuff shoes with packing paper to hold shape. Pack in original boxes or pair them in zip-locks. Don't pack dirty shoes with clean clothes. |
| CL-3 | Linens: extra sheets, pillowcases, tablecloths | Vacuum-seal bags or use as padding. |
| CL-4 | Holiday and seasonal decor | Wrap ornaments individually. Use egg cartons for small delicate items. Mark "HOLIDAY" so you can stash the box without unpacking immediately. |
| CL-5 | Luggage (not in use) | Use empty luggage as packing containers — stuff them with soft items like scarves, belts, and hats. It's free box space. |
| CL-6 | Miscellaneous storage: board games, craft supplies, memorabilia | Bag loose pieces. Keep memorabilia in a waterproof bin, not a cardboard box. |

**🐕 Pet note:** Closets often hide old pet supplies — expired flea treatments, outgrown harnesses, chewed-up toys. Toss anything expired or damaged. Donate usable items to a shelter. Keep one backup leash and collar packed in CL-6 or the dog travel bag.

---

## 🔧 GARAGE / OUTDOOR / SHED

**Responsible:** M (me) — primary. Partner assists with heavy items.
**Estimated time:** 3–4 hours total (this room has the most declutter and the most hazmat decisions)
**Priority:** HIGH for declutter (this is usually 30–40% of a move's junk volume), MEDIUM for packing

---

### Declutter Pass (1–1.5 hrs)

- [ ] Pull everything into the driveway or yard and sort
- [ ] **Toss / recycle:** dried-up paint cans (take to hazardous waste, check your county's schedule), broken tools, stripped screws and bent nails, old rags, cracked plant pots, broken holiday lights, mystery hardware, rusty anything
- [ ] **Donate:** working tools you have duplicates of, sports equipment you've outgrown, planters, garden decor
- [ ] **Sell:** power tools, bikes, outdoor furniture, working lawn equipment
- [ ] **Leave behind or sell:** lawn mower, snow blower, bags of salt and sand (Oregon's climate is very different — you may not need snow gear depending on your destination)
- [ ] **Give to the next tenant or neighbors:** partially full propane tanks, leftover mulch, garden hoses in decent shape

**Declutter gut-check:** Garages are the graveyard of

# Garage / Outdoor / Shed (Continued)

---

**Declutter gut-check (continued):** Garages are the graveyard of "I'll fix this someday" projects. If the item has been sitting broken for 6+ months, you're not going to fix it in Oregon either. Let it go. Also remember: **movers will not transport hazardous materials.** That includes gasoline, propane, paint thinner, pesticides, fertilizer, pool chemicals, ammunition, and fireworks. You must dispose of these before the move or give them away.

---

### Early Pack — 4 to 6 weeks out (1–1.5 hrs)

| Box | Contents | Packing Tips |
|---|---|---|
| GA-1 | Hand tools: hammer, screwdrivers, pliers, wrenches, tape measure, level | Wrap sharp tools in towels or cardboard sheaths. Heavy — use a small box. Put your most-used basic toolkit aside for the car kit (you'll need a screwdriver, pliers, box cutter, and hammer on arrival). |
| GA-2 | Power tools: drill, sander, circular saw, jigsaw | Remove batteries and pack them separately — lithium batteries can be a fire risk in hot trucks. Wrap cords around tools and secure with velcro or zip-ties. Original cases are ideal. |
| GA-3 | Lawn and garden: trowels, pruners, garden gloves, pots, seeds | Clean soil off everything — Oregon has agricultural inspection concerns at some points. Dump potting soil and don't transport open bags of soil or mulch. |
| GA-4 | Sports and recreation: bikes, camping gear, fishing rods, ski equipment | Deflate bike tires slightly for altitude changes on the drive. Remove pedals and turn handlebars sideways to save truck space. Bag all small parts. Fishing rods go in hard cases or PVC tubes taped shut. |
| GA-5 | Seasonal items: holiday inflatables, extension cords, outdoor lights | Test lights before packing — no point in moving dead strands. Wrap each strand around a piece of cardboard to prevent tangling. |
| GA-6 | Automotive: jumper cables, jack, tire iron, washer fluid, car cleaning supplies | Keep jumper cables and a flashlight in the car, not the truck. Don't pack fluids in the moving truck — use them up, give them away, or dispose safely. |

---

### Final Pack — last week (1 hr)

| Box | Contents | Packing Tips |
|---|---|---|
| GA-7 | Workbench items: vise, clamps, sandpaper, hardware organizer | Hardware organizers with small drawers — tape every drawer shut individually with painter's tape. If even one pops open, you'll spend an hour on your knees picking up screws. |
| GA-8 | Shelving, pegboard hooks, wall-mounted storage hardware | Zip-lock all mounting hardware. Photograph your pegboard layout if you want to replicate it. |
| GA-9 | Last items: broom, dustpan, step stool, vacuum, mop | Keep the broom and dustpan out until the final sweep. Literally the last things to load. Empty and clean the vacuum — you don't want Ohio dust mites starting a new life in Oregon. |

### Large Garage Items — No Box Needed

| Item | Tip |
|---|---|
| Bicycles | Remove pedals, turn handlebars, deflate tires slightly. Wrap chains in a rag so they don't grease other items. Load upright in the truck and strap down. |
| Workbench | Empty completely. If it disassembles, take it apart and bag hardware. If it doesn't, wrap legs and edges. |
| Shelving units | Disassemble. Bundle shelves with cardboard between them. Bag and label hardware for each unit separately. |
| Grill | Clean thoroughly. Remove propane tank and do not transport it — give it away or exchange it in Oregon. Tape lid shut. Wrap in a moving blanket. |
| Lawn mower | Drain all fuel and oil completely. Disconnect spark plug. Movers and truck rental companies will refuse to load it with fuel. If it's a cheap push mower, consider selling it and buying new in Oregon — the shipping cost may exceed its value. |
| Ladders | Load along the truck wall and strap down. Good for creating a wall-brace for other items. |
| Trash cans and recycling bins | Clean them. Use them as packing containers for unbreakable items like garden tools, brooms, and sports equipment. Free box space. |

**🐕 Pet note:** Garages often store dog crates, travel kennels, outdoor tie-outs, spare leashes, and large bags of food. Decide now whether the crate is coming (yes if you use it regularly or for travel). Pack the crate last — it may ride in the car for the dog. If you have a large bag of food that's mostly full, pour portions into zip-lock bags for the road trip and pack the rest sealed in a box labeled "DOG — OPEN FIRST." Dispose of old or recalled food.

---

## 🧺 LAUNDRY / UTILITY ROOM

**Responsible:** P (partner)
**Estimated time:** 1–1.5 hours total (mostly final-week work)
**Priority:** LOW-MEDIUM — small room, but appliance prep matters if you're moving your washer and dryer

---

### Declutter Pass (20 min)

- [ ] Pull everything off shelves and out of cabinets
- [ ] **Toss:** single socks (the other one isn't coming back), stretched-out dryer sheets, empty detergent bottles, clogged iron, stained ironing board cover, wire hangers in bulk, lint roller sheets that are all used up
- [ ] **Donate:** cleaning supplies you won't finish, working small appliances you don't want (steamer, spare iron)
- [ ] **Leave for the next tenant:** partially full bottles of detergent, dryer sheets, stain remover, fabric softener — not worth the weight

**Declutter gut-check:** This room accumulates supplies faster than any other. If you have 4 partial bottles of detergent, consolidate into one and leave the rest. Moving liquids is heavy, leak-prone, and not worth it.

---

### Early Pack — 4 to 6 weeks out (15–20 min)

| Box | Contents | Packing Tips |
|---|---|---|
| LU-1 | Spare cleaning supplies, broom attachments, mop heads, rags | Only pack sealed items in the truck. Use rags as packing padding elsewhere. |
| LU-2 | Iron, steamer, drying rack, lint rollers, sewing kit | Wrap the iron's soleplate in a towel. Empty any water reservoir. Coil cords. |

---

### Final Pack — last 2 to 3 days (30–45 min)

| Box | Contents | Packing Tips |
|---|---|---|
| LU-3 | Laundry baskets, hampers | Use these as packing containers — fill with soft items like towels, rags, stuffed animals, or dog bedding. Free box space. |
| LU-4 | Remaining detergent, dryer balls, stain pen | Zip-lock all liquids. Only bring what's sealed and worth the space. |
| LU-LAST | Cleaning supplies you used for move-out cleaning | These are literally the last things you pack. Keep a spray bottle, paper towels, trash bags, broom, and dustpan out until you walk out the door. Consider leaving them for the next tenant. |

### Appliance Notes (Washer and Dryer)

| Item | Tip |
|---|---|
| Washer | **48 hours before move:** Run an empty cycle. Disconnect and drain hoses completely. Leave the door open to air-dry the drum. **On move day:** Install transit bolts if you have them (they prevent the drum from moving in transit — check your manual or look up your model). Tape the power cord to the back. Tape the door shut. Move upright only. |
| Dryer | Disconnect and clean the lint trap and exhaust hose. Tape the door shut. Tape the cord to the back. If gas, have the gas line professionally disconnected. |
| Hot water heater | You're almost certainly not moving this — it stays with the house. Confirm with your landlord. |
| Furnace filters | Leave a clean one for the next tenant. Buy one for the Oregon place and have it ready. |

**🐕 Pet note:** If you wash the dog's bedding and blankets regularly, do one final wash 2 days before the move so the dog has a clean, familiar-smelling blanket for the car ride. Don't wash it with heavy scent detergent — the familiar smell is the point.

---
---

# 📋 DECLUTTER CHECKLIST TEMPLATE (Google Docs)

*Copy and paste this paragraph into a Google Doc. Duplicate it for each room.*

---

**Room: [ROOM NAME] — Declutter Checklist**
Pull everything out of every drawer, shelf, cabinet, and storage area in this room. Sort into four piles: **KEEP** (pack it), **DONATE** (working, clean, useful — schedule a drop-off or pickup), **SELL** (worth $20+ and you have time to list it on Marketplace, Craigslist, or Nextdoor), and **TRASH/RECYCLE** (broken, expired, stained, incomplete, or not worth anyone's time). For every item in the KEEP pile, ask: *"Have I used this in the last 12 months? Would I buy it again today? Is it worth the cost per pound to ship 2,400 miles?"* If the answer to all three is no, move it to DONATE or TRASH. Take a photo of the room before and after the declutter pass. Note anything you need to buy for the new place. Bag and label DONATE items immediately so they don't creep back into the KEEP pile. Schedule a donation pickup or drop-off date and put it on the calendar. Done is better than perfect — if you're agonizing over an item for more than 30 seconds, it goes.

These are estimates based on a typical 2BR apartment or small house for two adults. Adjust up if you have a lot of books, collections, or kitchen gear. Adjust down if you declutter aggressively (which I recommend — every box you eliminate saves $3–$8 in moving costs and 10–15 minutes of packing and unpacking time).

---

### Estimated Box Count by Room

| Room | Small (1.5 cu ft / "book box") | Medium (3.0 cu ft) | Large (4.5 cu ft) | Specialty | Total |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Kitchen | 4–5 | 4–5 | 1–2 | 1 dish-pack box | 10–13 |
| Living Room | 2–3 | 3–4 | 2–3 | 1 TV box (if no original box) | 8–11 |
| Master Bedroom | 1–2 | 2–3 | 2–3 | 2–3 wardrobe boxes | 7–11 |
| Bathroom(s) | 1–2 | 1–2 | 0 | — | 2–4 |
| Office / Study | 3–4 | 2–3 | 1 | 1 monitor box (if no original) | 7–9 |

| **TOTALS** | **14–22** | **17–25** | **9–15** | **4–6** | **~45–75 boxes** |

**Rule of thumb:** Most 2-bedroom moves land around 50–60 boxes with moderate decluttering. If you're aggressive declutterers, you might hit 40. If you're collectors or have a packed garage, budget for 75+.

# Room-by-Room Packing Checklist with Declutter Guide

---

## Universal "Donate / Sell / Keep / Trash" Decision Guide

Before you touch a single box, run every item through this filter:

| Question | If YES → | If NO → |
|---|---|---|
| Have I used this in the last 12 months? | Lean **keep** | Move to next question |
| Would I buy this again at full price today? | **Keep** | Lean **donate/sell** |
| Is it sentimental and irreplaceable? | **Keep**, but photograph bulk items and keep only the best | **Donate/sell** |
| Is it broken, stained, expired, or missing parts? | **Trash** (or recycle) | Move to next question |
| Could someone else genuinely use this? | **Donate** | **Trash/recycle** |
| Is it worth more than ~$25 and easy to sell? | **Sell** (FB Marketplace, Craigslist, consignment) | **Donate** |
| Am I keeping it "just in case"? | That's a no — **donate/sell** | — |

**Power rule:** If you haven't decided in 10 seconds, it goes in the donate box. You won't miss it in Oregon.

---

## Room 1: Kitchen

**Estimated time:** 6–8 hours (longest room)
**Priority:** Pack non-essentials early (Weeks 6–4). Pack daily-use items last week.
**Boxes:** 12–20 medium boxes, 3–5 small "heavy" boxes (for canned goods, cookbooks)
**Special supplies:** Packing paper (not newspaper — ink transfers), dish barrel boxes (tall, double-walled), cell dividers for glasses, Ziploc bags for utensil sets and hardware

### Checklist

**Early pack (Weeks 6–4):**
- [ ] Specialty appliances (bread maker, stand mixer, fondue pot, etc.)
- [ ] Bakeware you don't use weekly
- [ ] China, serving platters, holiday dishes
- [ ] Cookbooks
- [ ] Extra utensils and gadgets (second spatula drawer, we all have one)
- [ ] Vases, decorative items on top of cabinets
- [ ] Spices older than 1 year → **trash** (they've lost flavor)

**Mid pack (Weeks 3–2):**
- [ ] Most pots and pans (keep one skillet, one pot)
- [ ] Most dishes and glasses (keep 2 plates, 2 bowls, 2 cups, 2 sets of utensils per person)
- [ ] Small appliances (toaster, blender) — keep one coffee maker unpacked
- [ ] Food pantry: use it up, donate unopened non-perishables, trash anything expired

**Last pack (final 2 days):**
- [ ] Daily dishes, coffee maker, dish soap, sponge, trash bags, paper towels
- [ ] Fridge contents → cooler for the road or donate/discard
- [ ] Defrost freezer 24 hrs before move

**Declutter targets:**
- Duplicate utensils and gadgets (you don't need 4 whisks in Oregon)
- Chipped or mismatched dishes
- Expired food, old spices, mystery freezer items
- Takeout menus, plastic bags, rubber band collections
- Worn-out towels and potholders → donate to animal shelters

---

## Room 2: Living Room / Family Room

**Estimated time:** 3–5 hours
**Priority:** Decor and shelves early. Electronics and furniture last week.
**Boxes:** 5–10 medium boxes, 2–4 large boxes (pillows, blankets)
**Special supplies:** Bubble wrap for framed art, TV box or TV moving kit (available at U-Haul), furniture blankets, Ziploc bags for remote batteries and cords, cord labels or painter's tape

### Checklist

**Early pack (Weeks 6–4):**
- [ ] Books (small boxes — they get heavy fast, never fill a large box with books)
- [ ] DVDs, CDs, vinyl, games
- [ ] Decorative items, candles, picture frames
- [ ] Extra throw pillows and blankets

**Mid pack (Weeks 3–2):**
- [ ] Bookshelf contents, board games, puzzles
- [ ] Wall art and mirrors (wrap in bubble wrap, mark FRAGILE, transport vertically)
- [ ] Lamps (remove bulbs and shades, wrap shades in paper, never stack them)

**Last pack (final 2 days):**
- [ ] TV — photograph the cable setup on the back before unplugging. Label every cord with painter's tape.
- [ ] Streaming devices, gaming consoles, routers
- [ ] Remotes (Ziploc bag, labeled)
- [ ] Couch cushions (use as padding in the truck or large trash bags for transport)
- [ ] Curtains and rods

**Declutter targets:**
- Books you won't reread → donate to Little Free Library or used bookstore
- Old magazines, catalogs
- Tangled or mystery cords → if you don't know what they charge, trash them
- DVDs for movies available on streaming
- Worn-out pillows, throws with pet damage beyond saving

---

## Room 3: Primary Bedroom

**Estimated time:** 3–4 hours
**Priority:** Off-season clothes and decor early. Bed and daily clothes last.
**Boxes:** 5–8 medium, 2–3 wardrobe boxes (worth the cost for suits, dresses, coats)
**Special supplies:** Wardrobe boxes, vacuum-seal bags for bulky bedding, mattress bag, Ziploc bags for small hardware

### Checklist

**Early pack (Weeks 6–4):**
- [ ] Off-season clothing
- [ ] Extra bedding sets, decorative pillows
- [ ] Jewelry you don't wear daily (carry valuables with you, not in the truck)
- [ ] Wall art, nightstand decor

**Mid pack (Weeks 3–2):**
- [ ] Most clothing → wardrobe boxes or leave on hangers and wrap in trash bags (poor man's wardrobe box)
- [ ] Dresser contents (you can leave lightweight clothes in drawers if the movers allow it — ask first)
- [ ] Shoes (keep one pair of walking/moving shoes out)
- [ ] Books, bedside items

**Last pack (final 2 days):**
- [ ] Sheets and pillows from the bed (put in a labeled trash bag for quick setup in Oregon)
- [ ] Alarm clock, phone chargers, daily toiletries
- [ ] Disassemble bed frame. Put hardware in a labeled Ziploc bag and tape it to the frame.
- [ ] Mattress into mattress bag

**Declutter targets:**
- Clothes that don't fit, are stained, or haven't been worn in 12+ months
- Wire hangers → return to dry cleaner or recycle
- Old pillows (replace every 1–2 years anyway)
- Worn-out shoes
- Dresser-top clutter (old receipts, coins → deposit, random items)

---

## Room 4: Bathroom(s)

**Estimated time:** 1–2 hours per bathroom
**Priority:** Easy room. Pack extras early, daily items last day.
**Boxes:** 2–4 small/medium boxes
**Special supplies:** Ziploc bags for liquids (they leak), small box for medicines, trash bag for shower curtain

### Checklist

**Early pack (Weeks 6–4):**
- [ ] Backup toiletries, hotel-size collections, rarely used products
- [ ] Guest towels, decorative items
- [ ] First aid supplies (consolidate into one kit)
- [ ] Cleaning supplies you won't need again (or use them up)

**Mid pack (Weeks 3–2):**
- [ ] Most towels (keep 2 per person + 1 dog towel)
- [ ] Hair tools you don't use daily
- [ ] Under-sink items

**Last pack (moving morning):**
- [ ] Daily toiletries → into your personal bag for the car, NOT the truck
- [ ] Shower curtain and rings
- [ ] Bath mat
- [ ] Toilet paper (leave one roll and pack one for the car — you will need it on the road)
- [ ] Trash can

**Declutter targets:**
- Expired medications (drop at a pharmacy take-back, don't flush)
- Dried-up nail polish, old makeup, travel-size empties
- Worn-out towels → animal shelter donation
- Products you tried once and hated

---

## Room 5: Home Office / Study

**Estimated time:** 3–5 hours
**Priority:** Paper purge early. Electronics and daily work setup last.
**Boxes:** 4–8 medium, 1–2 small for cables
**Special supplies:** Banker's boxes for files, anti-static bubble wrap for electronics, cord labels, Ziploc bags

### Checklist

**Early pack (Weeks 6–4):**
- [ ] Archive files older than 3 years (scan what you can, shred what you don't need)
- [ ] Books, reference materials
- [ ] Supplies you don't use (old ink cartridges, random cables)
- [ ] Decorative items, diplomas, art

**Mid pack (Weeks 3–2):**
- [ ] Printer (remove ink cartridges, bag them separately)
- [ ] Non-daily reference files
- [ ] Desk supplies

**Last pack (final 2 days):**
- [ ] Computer, monitor → original boxes if you have them, otherwise double-wrap
- [ ] Keyboard, mouse, webcam
- [ ] Chargers and daily cables
- [ ] Photograph the cable routing behind your desk before unplugging
- [ ] Router and modem (return rental equipment to the ISP, or pack your own)

**Declutter targets:**
- Old tax returns beyond 7 years → shred
- Outdated manuals (most are online now)
- Dead pens, dried markers, sticky notes from 2019
- Old business cards
- Cables and adapters for devices you no longer own

---

## Room 6: Garage / Storage / Attic / Basement

**Estimated time:** 4–8 hours (second longest — it's where things go to hide)
**Priority:** START HERE for decluttering. This room has the highest donate/trash ratio.
**Boxes:** 5–10 heavy-duty boxes, plus bins you already own
**Special supplies:** Heavy-duty trash bags, work gloves, labels for hazmat items

### Checklist

**Early pack (Weeks 8–6):**
- [ ] Holiday decorations (consolidate into fewer bins)
- [ ] Camping, sports, and hobby gear
- [ ] Tools you'll keep (wrap sharp edges)
- [ ] Off-season outdoor items

**Mid pack (Weeks 3–2):**
- [ ] Remaining storage bins and boxes
- [ ] Luggage (use luggage as packing containers — fill suitcases with stuff)

**Last pack (final days):**
- [ ] Lawn and garden tools — decide what's worth moving 2,400 miles
- [ ] Workbench and pegboard items
- [ ] Ladders, shelving (disassemble)

**⚠️ Hazmat — cannot go in a moving truck:**
- Propane tanks, gasoline, lighter fluid
- Paint, paint thinner, solvents
- Pesticides, fertilizers, pool chemicals
- Ammunition (some movers allow; ask)
- Car batteries

**Dispose of these properly** at your county hazardous waste center or during a local collection event. Do NOT pack them.

**Declutter targets — be ruthless here:**
- Broken tools, rusty hardware
- Paint cans older than 2 years (they're probably bad)
- Boxes of "I'll fix this someday" items
- Duplicate garden tools
- Furniture you stored because you didn't want to deal with it
- Kids' outgrown gear (if applicable)

---

## Room 7: Laundry / Utility Room

**Estimated time:** 1–2 hours
**Priority:** Easy. Pack cleaning supplies last.
**Boxes:** 1–3 small/medium
**Special supplies:** Trash bags, Ziploc bags for loose items

### Checklist

- [ ] Disconnect and clean the washer. Run an empty hot cycle with vinegar. Leave the door open to dry.
- [ ] Clean the dryer lint trap and vent.
- [ ] Pack laundry supplies (or use them up and buy new in Oregon — detergent is heavy)
- [ ] Ironing board and iron
- [ ] Mops, brooms, vacuum → decide: move or replace?
- [ ] Keep one all-purpose cleaner, paper towels, and trash bags for the final clean

**Declutter targets:**
- Nearly empty bottles of cleaner
- Stained or torn cleaning rags
- Lone socks (the other one isn't coming back)
- Old iron or steamer you never use

---

## Room 8: Outdoor / Patio / Balcony

**Estimated time:** 1–3 hours
**Priority:** Early. Outdoor furniture is bulky and heavy — decide what's worth moving.
**Boxes:** Minimal. Most outdoor items are loose-load.
**Special supplies:** Furniture covers, bungee cords, disassembly tools

### Checklist

- [ ] Patio furniture → sell or move? A $150 patio set costs $200+ to ship. Buy new in Oregon?
- [ ] Grill → empty propane and sell/donate. Propane tanks cannot ship.
- [ ] Planters, garden tools, hoses
- [ ] Outdoor lights and decor
- [ ] Doormat → leave or toss (they're $10 new)
- [ ] Bikes → measure the truck space or ship separately

**Declutter targets:**
- Weathered furniture not worth moving
- Broken pots, dead plants
- Garden chemicals (hazmat)
- Hoses with leaks

---

## Packing Pro Tips (All Rooms)

1. **Label every box on the top AND one side** with room name + brief contents + FRAGILE if needed
2. **Number your boxes** and keep a running inventory on your phone (Notes app or Google Sheet). If a box goes missing, you'll know what was in it.
3. **Heavy items in small boxes, light items in large boxes.** Your back and your movers will thank you.
4. **Fill empty space** with packing paper, towels, or clothing. Rattling = breaking.
5. **Wrap plates vertically** like records, not stacked flat. They survive impacts better on edge.
6. **Photograph inside each box** before taping it shut.
7. **Keep hardware with its furniture.** Ziploc bag taped to the piece, every time.
8. **Don't pack the packing supplies last.** Keep tape, markers, paper, and scissors accessible until the final box.

# 6–8 WEEK CALENDAR OF REMINDERS

Below is a week-by-week schedule you can drop into Google Calendar, Apple Reminders, or any app. Each item is written as a standalone reminder with a suggested day. Adjust the actual dates to your move date and set alerts for 9 AM so you have the full day to act.

**How to use:** Count back from your move date. If your move date is a Saturday, Week 1 Monday is the Monday of that week. Week 8 Monday is 8 Mondays before that.

---

## WEEK 8 (8 weeks before move day)

**Monday**
- Get 3–4 moving company quotes OR reserve a rental truck/container. Verify USDOT numbers.

**Tuesday**
- Check lease notice requirement. Draft and send written notice to landlord today if 60-day notice is required.

**Wednesday**
- Research Oregon rental listings and neighborhoods. Set up search alerts on Zillow, Apartments.com, Craigslist.

**Thursday**
- Schedule vet visit for the dog: health check, vaccine records, rabies certificate copy.

**Friday**
- Start the Documents Folder: gather IDs, titles, insurance cards, lease, tax records. Put them in one place.

---

## WEEK 7

**Monday**
- Compare mover quotes and vehicle shipping quotes. Make a decision this week.

**Tuesday**
- Book the mover or truck. Read the contract and confirm valuation coverage.

**Wednesday**
- If shipping a vehicle: book the carrier. Confirm open vs. enclosed and pickup window.

**Thursday**
- Book temporary housing in Oregon (dog-friendly Airbnb or extended-stay) if your new place won't be ready on arrival.

**Friday**
- Call Oregon utility providers: electric, gas, water, trash. Ask about lead times. Schedule internet installation NOW.

---

## WEEK 6

**Monday**
- Begin the Great Declutter. Start with the garage, storage unit, and junk drawers. Decide: keep, sell, donate, trash.

**Tuesday**
- List sellable items on Facebook Marketplace, Craigslist, or Nextdoor. Price to move fast.

**Wednesday**
- Order packing supplies: boxes (small, medium, large, wardrobe), packing tape, bubble wrap, markers, paper.

**Thursday**
- Notify your employer and partner's employer of the move date. Ask about remote work, relocation assistance, and payroll address changes.

**Friday**
- Sign the Oregon lease or confirm closing date. Save a copy of the lease or contract to your Move folder.

---

## WEEK 5

**Monday**
- Pack Room 1: Guest bedroom, storage room, or least-used space. Label every box with room name and contents.

**Tuesday**
- Pack Room 2: Office, books, decor, wall art. Wrap frames in towels.

**Wednesday**
- Schedule donation pickups (Habitat ReStore, Goodwill, Salvation Army) for next week.

**Thursday**
- Send landlord formal written move-out notice if you haven't yet (30-day deadline). Request a move-out inspection.

**Friday**
- Notify banks, credit cards, and insurance companies of your upcoming address change. Set the effective date for move day.

---

## WEEK 4

**Monday**
- File change of address with USPS at usps.com. Set the start date for ~2 days before your move.

**Tuesday**
- Schedule Ohio utility shutoffs (electric, gas, water, trash, cable/internet) for the day after you leave.

**Wednesday**
- Confirm Oregon utility start dates. Confirm internet install appointment.

**Thursday**
- Pack Room 3: Kitchen — non-essentials (specialty appliances, baking supplies, extra dishes, cookbooks). Keep one pot, one pan, basic utensils, and plates for two until the last day.

**Friday**
- Cancel or transfer subscriptions and memberships: gym, CSA box, newspaper, streaming services tied to location, library cards. See if anything has an early termination fee.

---

## WEEK 3

**Monday**
- Pack Room 4: Living room — books, games, decor, media, seasonal items. Leave the couch, one lamp, and a screen for the last week.

**Tuesday**
- Pack Room 5: Bathroom — extras (towels, cleaning supplies, backup toiletries). Keep one set of towels and daily toiletries out.

**Wednesday**
- Confirm mover: arrival time, crew size, payment method, final estimate in writing. OR confirm truck/container pickup time.

**Thursday**
- Car maintenance check: oil, tires, brakes, battery, fluids, wipers. Top off or schedule service.

**Friday**
- Research Oregon DMV requirements: documents needed for license, vehicle registration, emissions test (if Portland metro). Write a checklist and put it in the Move folder.

---

## WEEK 2

**Monday**
- Pack Room 6: Master bedroom — off-season clothes, extra bedding, nightstand items. Leave sheets, pillows, and 3 days of clothes.

**Tuesday**
- Finish selling or donating remaining declutter items. Put unsold items at the curb or schedule bulk trash pickup.

**Wednesday**
- Pack the dog travel kit: leash, harness, food (5+ days), bowls, meds, records, blanket, toy, poop bags, paper towels. Keep it accessible.

**Thursday**
- Get a new ID tag for the dog with your phone number. Confirm all overnight lodging along the route is booked and dog-friendly.

**Friday**
- Do a dress rehearsal: lay out the Moving Day Essentials list and check every item. Charge the power bank. Load the cooler and snacks the night before.

---

## WEEK 1

**Monday**
- Pack the last of everything except what you'll use today through move day. Label boxes clearly.

**Tuesday**
- Defrost and clean the fridge and freezer. Donate or eat all perishable food.

**Wednesday**
- Take photos of all valuables, serial numbers, and the condition of your current home (every room, closets, floors, walls).

**Thursday (day before move)**
- Finish packing. Set aside the overnight bags and dog kit. Confirm the mover's arrival time or pick up the truck. Load the car with essentials tonight.

**Friday (MOVE DAY — adjust to your actual day)**
- Walk-through every room, closet, cabinet, attic, garage.
- Photograph utility meters.
- Meet movers, review inventory, sign Bill of Lading.
- Hand over keys, remotes, fobs. Get a receipt.
- Load the dog last. Hit the road.

---

## WEEK +1 (first week in Oregon)

**Monday**
- Photograph the new place at move-in. Document any existing damage and send it to the landlord in writing.

**Tuesday**
- Confirm all utilities are on and working. Test internet. Locate breaker box, water shutoff, gas shutoff.

**Wednesday**
- Schedule Oregon DMV visit: bring proof of identity, proof of residency, vehicle title, insurance, and payment. Get your license and start the registration process.

**Thursday**
- Take the dog to the new Oregon vet. Transfer records. Ask about the county dog license.

**Friday**
- Update microchip registry, voter registration, remaining subscriptions, and anything you missed. Breathe. You made it.

---

## QUICK-IMPORT FORMAT

If you use **Google Calendar**, create a new calendar called "Move" and add each item above as an all-day event with a 9:00 AM notification. Color-code by category (housing = blue, packing = green, dog = orange, admin = yellow).

reply:
# ROOM-BY-ROOM PACKING & DECLUTTER CHECKLIST

---

## SYSTEM OVERVIEW (Use this for every room)

### Declutter Decision Flow

For every item, ask these four questions in order:

```
1. Have I used this in the last 12 months?
   → NO → Go to 2
   → YES → KEEP (unless it's cheap to replace and expensive to move)

2. Would I buy this again at full price?
   → NO → Go to 3
   → YES → KEEP

3. Is it worth more than $25 and in good condition?
   → YES → SELL (Facebook Marketplace, Craigslist, garage sale)
   → NO → Go to 4

4. Is it functional and clean?
   → YES → DONATE (Goodwill, Habitat ReStore, Buy Nothing group)
   → NO → TRASH / RECYCLE
```

**Rule of thumb:** If moving it costs more than replacing it, let it go. A $40 bookshelf that takes up truck space and weighs 60 lbs is not worth moving 2,400 miles.

---

### Labeling System

Write all three lines on **two sides** of every box in thick marker:

```
Line 1: ROOM NAME (e.g., KITCHEN)
Line 2: Contents summary (e.g., plates, bowls, mugs)
Line 3: Priority tag
```

**Priority tags:**
- **🔴 OPEN FIRST** — You need this within hours of arrival (sheets, towels, toilet paper, coffee maker, dog bowls)
- **🟡 OPEN SOON** — Need within 2–3 days (most clothes, basic cookware, office setup)
- **🟢 OPEN LATER** — Can wait a week or more (decor, books, seasonal, storage)
- **⚠️ FRAGILE** — Add this on top of any priority tag. Also write FRAGILE on the top and all four sides. Draw arrows pointing up.

**Color-coded tape (optional but powerful):** Assign a tape color to each room. When the movers or you unload, boxes go straight to the right room without reading labels.

| Room | Tape Color |
|---|---|
| Kitchen | Red |
| Master Bedroom | Blue |
| Living Room | Green |
| Office | Yellow |
| Bathroom | White |
| Garage / Storage | Orange |

---

### Fragile Packing Tips (Reference for Every Room)

- **Plates:** Stand on edge vertically in small boxes, never flat-stacked. Wrap each plate in packing paper or a dish towel. Place crumpled paper between them.
- **Glasses and mugs:** Stuff the inside with paper, wrap the outside, place upside down in a box with dividers or a cell kit. Small boxes only.
- **Mirrors and frames:** Make an X with painter's tape across the glass (limits shatter spread). Wrap in bubble wrap, stand on edge in a box, never lay flat.
- **Electronics:** Use original boxes if you kept them. If not, wrap in bubble wrap, fill gaps with towels or packing paper. Photograph cable setups before disconnecting.
- **Lamps:** Remove shades and bulbs. Wrap the base in bubble wrap. Pack shades in separate boxes nested inside each other with paper between them.
- **Knives:** Wrap each blade in cardboard or several layers of paper. Tape the cardboard closed. Bundle them together and label SHARP.
- **Liquids:** Place in a zip-lock bag first, then pack upright. Tighten all lids. Consider tossing anything half-empty and cheap to replace.
- **General rule:** If you can hear items shifting when you gently shake the box, add more packing material. No rattling, no breaking.

---

## ROOM 1: KITCHEN

**Your inventory notes:** Lots of dishes, 3 small appliances, spice rack.

### Estimated Effort
| Metric | Estimate |
|---|---|
| Total boxes | 12–18 (mostly small and medium) |
| Suggested box mix | 8 small, 6 medium, 2 large, 1 dish-barrel if you have one |
| Time to declutter | 2–3 hours |
| Time to pack | 4–6 hours (the kitchen is always the longest room) |
| Recommended schedule | Declutter in Week 6. Pack non-essentials in Week 4. Pack the rest the day before. |

### Declutter First

| Category | Keep | Sell / Donate | Trash |
|---|---|---|---|
| Dishes and plates | One full set for your household size + a few extras | Duplicate sets, chipped pieces, novelty mugs you never use | Cracked, stained, or broken items |
| Glasses and mugs | Daily-use glasses + a few wine/beer glasses | Promotional cups, mismatched sets, excess travel mugs | Anything chipped |
| Cookware | 1 large pot, 1 small pot, 1 skillet, 1 baking sheet, 1 casserole dish | Duplicate pans, warped baking sheets, specialty items you used once | Scratched nonstick with flaking coating |
| Utensils and tools | 1 set of cooking utensils, 1 good knife set, can opener, peeler, spatula, tongs | Duplicate whisks, rusty tools, single-use gadgets (avocado slicer, banana cutter) | Broken or rusty items |
| Small appliances (3) | Keep the ones you use weekly | Sell or donate anything you haven't used in 6 months | Broken or missing parts |
| Spice rack | Keep spices less than 1 year old | — | Expired spices (smell test: if it smells like nothing, toss it) |
| Food and pantry | Sealed, non-perishable items you'll actually eat | Donate unopened canned goods and dry goods to a food bank | Expired food, open packages you won't finish |
| Cleaning supplies | 1 all-purpose cleaner, dish soap, sponge for move-out cleaning | — | Nearly empty bottles, duplicate products (cheaper to buy new in Oregon) |
| Tupperware and food storage | Matching sets with lids only | Lidless containers, excess takeout containers | Stained, warped, or melted items |

### Packing Order

**Pack in Week 4 (non-essentials):**
- [ ] Baking supplies and specialty bakeware
- [ ] Extra dish sets and serving platters
- [ ] Cookbooks
- [ ] Small appliances you won't use in the next 2 weeks (decide which one or two you keep out)
- [ ] Vases, decorative kitchen items
- [ ] Wine glasses and bar tools
- [ ] Spice rack (bag each jar in a zip-lock in case of leaks, pack upright in a small box)

**Pack in Week 2 (scaling down):**
- [ ] All remaining dishes except 2 plates, 2 bowls, 2 mugs, 2 glasses
- [ ] All pots and pans except 1 pot and 1 skillet
- [ ] All utensils except 2 forks, 2 knives, 2 spoons, 1 spatula, 1 cooking spoon
- [ ] Remaining small appliances except the coffee maker (or whatever you can't live without)
- [ ] Remaining pantry items (sealed, non-perishable)

**Pack last (day before or morning of move):**
- [ ] Coffee maker and daily mugs
- [ ] Last 2 plates, 2 bowls, 2 glasses
- [ ] Last pot, skillet, and utensils
- [ ] Dish soap, sponge, paper towels (keep paper towels for the car)
- [ ] Trash bags (keep a few for the car and for move-in)
- [ ] Cooler (load it with road snacks and drinks last)

### Kitchen Packing Tips
- **Heaviest items in small boxes.** Plates, cast iron, canned goods — small box, always.
- **Wrap every dish individually.** Use packing paper, newspaper (ink can transfer to white dishes), or dish towels and t-shirts as free padding.
- **Stand plates vertically** like records in a crate, not stacked flat.
- **Nesting:** Put small bowls inside large bowls with paper between them.
- **Knives:** Cardboard sleeve taped shut for each knife, or wrap the whole block.
- **Appliances:** Remove glass carafes and blades. Pack them separately and label them.
- **Under the sink:** Tighten every cap. Put each bottle in a zip-lock bag. Pack upright in a bin or small box lined with a trash bag.
- **Spice jars:** Rubber-band the lids, bag each jar, pack upright in a small box. Consider tossing and rebuying — spices are light but fragile and leak easily.

### Box Labels for This Room
```
KITCHEN — Plates, bowls (fragile) — 🔴 OPEN FIRST ⚠️ FRAGILE
KITCHEN — Pots, pans, baking — 🟡 OPEN SOON
KITCHEN — Coffee maker, mugs, utensils — 🔴 OPEN FIRST
KITCHEN — Spices, pantry dry goods — 🟡 OPEN SOON
KITCHEN — Bakeware, serving, cookbooks — 🟢 OPEN LATER
KITCHEN — Small appliances — 🟡 OPEN SOON
KITCHEN — Under-sink, cleaning supplies — 🟢 OPEN LATER
```

---

## ROOM 2: MASTER BEDROOM

### Estimated Effort
| Metric | Estimate |
|---|---|
| Total boxes | 8–12 |
| Suggested box mix | 2 small, 4 medium, 2 large, 2 wardrobe |
| Time to declutter | 1.5–2 hours |
| Time to pack | 2–3 hours |
| Recommended schedule | Declutter in Week 6. Pack non-essentials in Week 3. Pack the rest the morning of. |

### Declutter First

| Category | Keep | Sell / Donate | Trash |
|---|---|---|---|
| Clothing (your side) | Clothes you've worn in the last year, fits well, in good condition | Anything that doesn't fit, you haven't worn in a year, or makes you feel nothing | Stained, torn, worn-out items |
| Shoes | Daily pairs + 1 dress, 1 seasonal | Duplicates, uncomfortable pairs, worn-out soles | Broken or unwearable |
| Bedding | 2 sheet sets, 2 pillow sets, 1 comforter, 1 extra blanket | Excess flat sheets, old pillows (replace every 2 years), duplicate comforters | Stained, torn, or flat pillows |
| Nightstand items | Daily items, charger, book | — | Old receipts, dead batteries, broken items |
| Jewelry and accessories | Worn regularly or sentimental | Sell valuable pieces you don't wear | Broken costume jewelry |
| Under-bed storage | Evaluate each item using the decision flow | — | — |

### Packing Order

**Pack in Week 3:**
- [ ] Off-season clothing (winter coats if moving in summer, etc.) — use wardrobe boxes for hanging clothes
- [ ] Extra bedding and pillows (vacuum-seal bags save huge space)
- [ ] Books and decor from nightstands and dressers
- [ ] Under-bed storage items
- [ ] Wall art and mirrors (tape glass, wrap, stand on edge)
- [ ] Jewelry box (carry this in the car, not on the truck)

**Pack in Week 2:**
- [ ] Most remaining clothes, leaving 3 days of outfits and sleepwear
- [ ] Extra shoes
- [ ] Dresser drawers: you can leave soft clothes in dresser drawers if the movers allow it — wrap the dresser in stretch wrap to keep drawers shut

**Pack last (morning of move day):**
- [ ] Sheets and pillows (strip the bed, stuff them in a trash bag, label it, toss it in the car or on top of the truck load)
- [ ] Phone chargers and bedside items
- [ ] Last 3 days of clothes (already in your overnight bag)
- [ ] Hamper with dirty laundry (tie the bag shut, it goes on the truck — no need to wash first)

### Box Labels for This Room
```
MASTER BED — Sheets, pillows, blankets — 🔴 OPEN FIRST
MASTER BED — Hanging clothes (wardrobe box 1 of 2) — 🟡 OPEN SOON
MASTER BED — Off-season clothes — 🟢 OPEN LATER
MASTER BED — Shoes, accessories — 🟡 OPEN SOON
MASTER BED — Nightstand, books, decor — 🟢 OPEN LATER
MASTER BED — Wall art (fragile) — 🟢 OPEN LATER ⚠️ FRAGILE
```

---

## ROOM 3: PARTNER'S CLOSET

### Estimated Effort
| Metric | Estimate |
|---|---|
| Total boxes | 4–8 |
| Suggested box mix | 2 medium, 2 large, 2 wardrobe |
| Time to declutter | 1.5–2 hours |
| Time to pack | 1.5–2 hours |
| Recommended schedule | Declutter in Week 6. Pack in Week 3. Leave 3 days of clothes out. |

### Declutter First

Use the same clothing decision flow as the master bedroom. Partner owns this process — schedule a 2-hour block, put on music, and make it a focused session.

**Paper rule of thumb:** If you can access it digitally (bank statements, bills, insurance EOBs), shred the paper copy. Scan anything you're unsure about before shredding — use your phone camera or a free scanning app like Adobe Scan.

**Pack in Week 2:**

**Pack last (last working day or morning of move):**
- [ ] Computer / laptop and power cable → carry in the car, never on the truck
- [ ] Monitor — wrap in a towel, place in original box or between two pieces of cardboard taped together, then in a large box padded on all sides. If you have the original foam inserts, use them. Mark FRAGILE on every side.
- [ ] Mouse, keyboard, headset, and daily-use cables
- [ ] Modem and router (you may need internet until the last day — pack these after your last email check)
- [ ] External hard drive or backup drive → car, not the truck
- [ ] Any work files or documents you need access to during the drive

### Fragile Packing Tips — Office Specific
- **Monitor:** This is the most fragile item in the office. Original box is best. If you don't have it, make a cardboard sandwich: cut two pieces of cardboard larger than the screen, place the wrapped monitor between them, tape the cardboard together, then place the whole assembly in a large box with 3+ inches of padding on every side. Never lay a monitor face down.
- **Hard drives:** Wrap in bubble wrap and pack in a small box with padding. Better yet, carry them in a padded bag in the car. Temperature extremes and vibration can damage drives.

- **Cables:** Coil each cable individually and secure with a twist tie or velcro strap. Put all cables in one labeled zip-lock bag or small box. Photograph your desk cable setup before disconnecting.

### Fragile Packing Tips — Bathroom Specific

| Category | Keep | Sell / Donate | Trash |

| Hand tools | Quality tools you actually use: hammer, screwdrivers, pliers, wrenches, tape measure, level, drill | Duplicate or cheap tools, tools for projects you'll never do | Rusted, broken, dull beyond sharpening |
| Power tools | Drill, circular saw, or others you use regularly | Sell specialty tools you used once (Craigslist, Facebook) | Non-functional, missing parts |
| Lawn mower | **Decision point:** Will you have a yard in Oregon? If yes, is it cheaper to move or replace? A basic push mower costs $150–$300 new but takes significant truck space. | Sell if you're moving to an apartment or won't have a yard | — |
| Bikes (2) | Keep if you'll ride them in Oregon | Sell if they're unused or low-value | Rusted, flat-tired, not worth repairing |
| Storage bins | Open every bin and apply the decision flow to the contents. Keep the bins themselves only if they're in good shape. | Donate contents you don't need | Cracked or lidless bins |
| Hardware and fasteners | Consolidate into one small organizer: screws, nails, anchors, picture hangers, zip ties | Excess or project-specific hardware | Rusty, mixed junk drawers of mystery parts |
| Automotive supplies | Jumper cables, tire gauge, emergency kit, motor oil (1 qt for the drive) | Excess or old oil, coolant, brake fluid — take to an auto parts store for recycling, never trash | Dried-out rags, old wiper blades |
| Seasonal and holiday | Genuinely used decorations and items | Excess or duplicate holiday decorations | Broken lights, dried-out items, things you forgot you had |
| Paint and chemicals | **Do not move these on a truck.** Most movers won't take paint, solvents, propane tanks, gasoline, or aerosols. | Donate usable paint to Habitat ReStore | Dry out old paint cans and trash them per local rules. Take chemicals to a hazardous waste drop-off. |
| Gardening | Quality tools: shovel, rake, pruners, hose | Excess pots (heavy and cheap to replace), old soil bags | Broken or rusted tools |

### Lawn Mower Decision
- **If keeping:** Drain all fuel and oil before moving. Movers and truck rental companies do not allow fuel in transit. Run it dry or siphon the tank. Disconnect the spark plug. Clean the deck. Wrap the blade in cardboard. It goes loose on the truck, not in a box.
- **If selling:** List it 3–4 weeks before the move. Price it to sell fast — $50–$100 for a used push mower moves quickly.

### Bike Prep
- Remove pedals and turn handlebars sideways to reduce the footprint.
- If you have bike boxes (from a bike shop — ask, they usually give them away), use those.
- If not, wrap the frames in moving blankets or bubble wrap and secure with stretch wrap.
- Deflate tires slightly for altitude changes on mountain passes.
- Bikes go on the truck last (loaded first to come off first) or on a car-mounted bike rack.

### Packing Order

**Pack in Week 4:**
- [ ] Storage bins — open each one, declutter, repack keepers, label the bin with the new room destination
- [ ] Seasonal and holiday items
- [ ] Gardening tools and supplies
- [ ] Excess hardware and shop supplies

**Pack in Week 3:**
- [ ] Hand tools — wrap sharp edges in cardboard or towels, pack heavy tools in small boxes
- [ ] Power tools — remove batteries, wrap cords, use original cases if available, otherwise bubble wrap in medium boxes
- [ ] Remaining garage shelving contents

**Pack in Week 2:**
- [ ] Drain lawn mower fuel and oil. Clean and prep.
- [ ] Prep bikes (pedals off, handlebars turned, tires deflated)
- [ ] Dispose of paint, chemicals, propane tanks, old oil at hazardous waste drop-off
- [ ] Break down shelving if you're taking it. Bag all hardware in a zip-lock
